## Plan summary

Epic-scope task decomposed into **4 cohesive Stories** mapped to the four cooperating units, sliced along real architectural seams:

| # | Story | Wave | depends_on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| [#1](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-24-epic-scope-mandrel-0d05d92d/issues/1) | Shared on-disk store, schema, idempotent migrations (Unit 1) | 0 | — |
| [#2](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-24-epic-scope-mandrel-0d05d92d/issues/2) | JSON REST API: accounts, projects, tasks, export enqueue (Unit 2) | 1 | #1 |
| [#3](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-24-epic-scope-mandrel-0d05d92d/issues/3) | Operator admin CLI: stats + deactivate-user (Unit 4) | 1 | #1 |
| [#4](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-24-epic-scope-mandrel-0d05d92d/issues/4) | Background report worker + whole-platform `npm start` (Unit 3) | 2 | #1, #2 |

**Schedule:** wave 0 (store) → wave 1 (**API ∥ admin-CLI in parallel**) → wave 2 (worker + runtime). Parallelism yield 1.33.

**Key design decisions baked into the specs:**
- Store is the sole schema owner (SSOT) as the task mandates; it also scaffolds all `package.json` scripts (`migrate`/`start`/`admin`) so no two wave-1 stories co-edit `package.json` — preserving the API ∥ CLI parallelism.
- On-disk SQLite file (e.g. built-in `node:sqlite`), never in-memory; migrations idempotent + applied on API boot.
- Password hashing + bearer-token auth + owner-scoping (404 across users) + 400-on-malformed (never crash) as API invariants; deactivated-user login rejection owned by the API, the flag-flip owned by the CLI (keeps them decoupled → parallel).
- Export report produced **only** in the worker; `npm start` boots API + worker together; queued jobs survive restart.

**Gates:** Gate #1 and Gate #2 auto-proceeded under `--yes`. Both plan critics returned `dispatch: false`; text-hygiene clean. Persist dry-run passed all hard gates before the live write.

Soft findings noted and consciously accepted: two `spec-word-budget` advisories (274/338 words) and "thin dependent slice" flags — the latter is a false positive here since the store feeds three consumers (not a single-consumer feeder) and the wave table confirms genuine parallelism; each `reason_to_exist` carries its earn-its-slot justification.

Deliver later (separate session) with: `/deliver 1 2 3 4`.
